summary.de: Intensität nach MET: leicht ab 1,5, moderat ab 3, intensiv ab 6 MET.
summary.en: Intensity by MET: light from 1.5, moderate from 3, vigorous from 6 METs.

source.title: Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955

quote: On an absolute scale, light intensity refers to physical activity that is performed between 1.5 and 3 METs. […] moderate-intensity refers to the physical activity that is performed between 3 and <6 times the intensity of rest (METs). […] vigorous intensity refers to physical activity that is performed at 6.0 or more METs.

summary.de: Erwachsene (18–64): 150–300 Min. moderat oder 75–150 Min. intensiv pro Woche (oder eine gleichwertige Mischung) und an mindestens 2 Tagen Kräftigung aller großen Muskelgruppen.
summary.en: Adults (18–64): 150–300 min moderate or 75–150 min vigorous per week (or an equivalent mix), plus muscle strengthening of all major muscle groups on 2 or more days.

source.title: Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955

quote: Adults should do at least 150–300 min of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity, or at least 75–150 min of vigorous-intensity aerobic physical activity, or an equivalent combination of moderate-intensity and vigorous-intensity activity throughout the week for substantial health benefits; Adults should also do muscle-strengthening activities at moderate or greater intensity that involve all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week, as these provide additional health benefits.

summary.de: Ab 65: wie Erwachsene, plus an mindestens 3 Tagen vielseitige Aktivität mit Gleichgewicht und Kraft.
summary.en: 65 and older: as adults, plus varied multicomponent activity emphasising balance and strength on 3 or more days.

source.title: Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955

quote: As for adults, plus […] As part of their weekly physical activity, older adults should do varied multicomponent physical activity that emphasises functional balance and strength training at moderate or greater intensity on 3 or more days a week, to enhance functional capacity and to prevent falls.

summary.de: 5–17 Jahre: im Schnitt 60 Min. pro Tag moderat bis intensiv, an mindestens 3 Tagen intensiv sowie Muskel- und Knochenkräftigung.
summary.en: Ages 5–17: an average of 60 min a day moderate to vigorous, with vigorous and muscle- and bone-strengthening activity on at least 3 days.

source.title: Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955

quote: Children and adolescents should do at least an average of 60 min/day of moderate-to-vigorous intensity, mostly aerobic, physical activity, across the week; Vigorous-intensity aerobic activities, as well as those that strengthen muscle and bone should be incorporated at least 3 days a week.

summary.de: Etwas Bewegung ist besser als keine. Klein anfangen und Häufigkeit, Intensität und Dauer nach und nach steigern.
summary.en: Some activity is better than none. Start small and gradually increase frequency, intensity and duration.

source.title: Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955

quote: Some physical activity is better than none. If not currently meeting these recommendations, doing some physical activity will bring benefits to health. Start with small amounts of physical activity and gradually increase frequency, intensity and duration over time.

summary.de: Jede Dauer zählt: auch kurze Einheiten unter 10 Minuten zählen zum Wochenziel.
summary.en: Every bout counts: sessions shorter than 10 minutes count towards the weekly target too.

source.title: Bull FC et al. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. Br J Sports Med 2020;54:1451–1462. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955

quote: MVPA bouts of any duration now count towards these recommendations, reflecting new evidence to support the value of total physical activity volume, regardless of bout length. This recommendation differs from the requirement of bouts of at least 10 min in the previous WHO 2010 guidelines.

summary.de: Radfahren und Schwimmen sind Sportarten ohne Stoßbelastung (geringer Impact).
summary.en: Cycling and swimming are non-impact sports (low impact).

source.title: Gómez-Bruton A, González-Agüero A, et al. Is bone tissue really affected by swimming? A systematic review. PLoS One 2013;8(8):e70119. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0070119

quote: Recent literature reviews have shown that high impact sports seem to be more osteogenic than non impact sports such as swimming or cycling, in children [12] , young adults [12] or older adults [13] .

summary.de: Laufen zählt in den Studien dieser Übersicht als mittlere, wiederholte Stoßbelastung.
summary.en: Running counts as medium, repetitive impact in the studies of this review.

source.title: Gómez-Bruton A, González-Agüero A, et al. Is bone tissue really affected by swimming? A systematic review. PLoS One 2013;8(8):e70119. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0070119

quote: MED = Medium impact (running and field hockey) […] REP = Repetitive impact sports(running)

summary.de: Wer vor allem Rad fährt, profitiert für die Knochen von einer Aktivität mit Stoßbelastung (z. B. Laufen).
summary.en: People who mainly cycle benefit their bones from an activity with impact (e.g. running).

source.title: Olmedillas H, González-Agüero A, et al. Cycling and bone health: a systematic review. BMC Med 2012;10:168. doi:10.1186/1741-7015-10-168

quote: Based on the available evidence, in general, cycling as a sole form of exercise is not recommended for people who are at risk of developing osteoporosis, unless it is complemented with some kind of osteogenic training. […] Beatty et al. [ 56 ] and Nichols et al. [ 42 ] proposed to incorporate impact activities in training programs for cyclists

summary.de: Schwimmen schadet den Knochen nicht, baut sie aber kaum auf: eine Aktivität mit Stoßbelastung ergänzt es.
summary.en: Swimming does not harm bones but builds little bone: an activity with impact complements it.

source.title: Gómez-Bruton A, González-Agüero A, et al. Is bone tissue really affected by swimming? A systematic review. PLoS One 2013;8(8):e70119. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0070119

quote: Swimming does not seem to negatively affect bone mass, although it may not be one of the best sports to be practised in order to increase this parameter, due to the hypogravity and lack of impact characteristic of this sport.

summary.de: Mountainbiken belastet Nacken, Hand/Handgelenk, unteren Rücken und Knie; Krafttraining (neben Bike-Fitting) kann Überlastung vorbeugen.
summary.en: Mountain biking strains neck, hand/wrist, lower back and knees; strength training (besides bike fit) may help prevent overuse.

source.title: Arriel RA, Souza HLR, et al. Current perspectives of cross-country mountain biking: physiological and mechanical aspects, evolution of bikes, accidents and injuries. Int J Environ Res Public Health 2022;19(19):12552. doi:10.3390/ijerph191912552

quote: The main syndromes affect the neck, hand/wrist, low back and knees [ 76 ]. […] Bike fit (i.e., bike adjustment according to the cyclist’s profile), correction of riding style, bicycle settings (such as suspension system) and resistance training seem to be an alternative to reduce such risks [ 77 ].

summary.de: Nach 4–6 Wochen Krafttraining kann eine Entlastungswoche (~7 Tage, weniger Umfang) angeboten werden. Expertenkonsens aus dem Kraftsport.
summary.en: After 4–6 weeks of strength training a deload week (~7 days, less volume) may be offered. Expert consensus from strength sports.

source.title: Bell L, Strafford BW, et al. Integrating deloading into strength and physique sports training programmes: an international Delphi consensus approach. Sports Med Open 2023;9:87. doi:10.1186/s40798-023-00633-0

quote: “Deloading is a period of reduced training stress designed to mitigate physiological and psychological fatigue, promote recovery, and enhance preparedness for subsequent training.” […] Deloading is generally undertaken every 4–6 weeks for a period of ~ 7 days, although some deloads might range in duration from a singular training session to 2 weeks [ 22 ].

summary.de: Für Steigerungen pro Woche gibt es keine belegte Obergrenze (auch nicht die „10 %-Regel“): langsam steigern, Steigerungen nur anbieten.
summary.en: There is no proven weekly increase limit (not even the "10% rule"): increase gradually and only offer increases.

source.title: Fredette A, Roy JS, et al. The association between running injuries and training parameters: a systematic review. J Athl Train 2022;57(7):650. doi:10.4085/1062-6050-0195.21

quote: Despite high rates of RRIs, current evidence does not consistently link RRIs with specific training parameters or recent changes in training parameters. Therefore, caution should be taken when recommending optimal parameters or progressions.

summary.de: Kraft nimmt zu mit mindestens 2 Krafteinheiten pro Woche (eher schwere Lasten, voller Bewegungsumfang, 2–3 Sätze).
summary.en: Strength improves with at least 2 strength sessions a week (heavier loads, full range of motion, 2–3 sets).

source.title: Currier BS, D'Souza AC, Fiatarone Singh MA, et al. American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance training prescription for muscle function, hypertrophy, and physical performance in healthy adults: an overview of reviews. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2026;58(4):851–872. doi:10.1249/MSS.0000000000003897

quote: However, voluntary strength was enhanced by lifting heavier loads (≥80% one-repetition maximum), through a complete range of motion, for 2–3 sets, at the beginning of training sessions, and ≥2 sessions/wk.

summary.de: Training mit dem eigenen Körpergewicht zählt als Krafttraining; die Art der Ausrüstung machte keinen beständigen Unterschied.
summary.en: Training with your own body weight counts as strength training; the type of equipment made no consistent difference.

source.title: Currier BS, D'Souza AC, Fiatarone Singh MA, et al. American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance training prescription for muscle function, hypertrophy, and physical performance in healthy adults: an overview of reviews. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2026;58(4):851–872. doi:10.1249/MSS.0000000000003897

quote: Resistance training (RT), also known as strength or weight training, is a specialized method of physical conditioning in which muscles are exercised by contracting against external resistance, such as free weights, machines, resistance bands, water, or body weight […] Training to momentary muscle fatigue, equipment type, exercise complexity, set structure, time under tension, blood flow restriction, and periodization did not consistently impact training outcomes.

summary.de: Bekannte Herz-Kreislauf-, Stoffwechsel- (Diabetes) oder Nierenerkrankung: vor dem Start ärztlich abklären.
summary.en: Known cardiovascular, metabolic (diabetes) or renal disease: get medical clearance before starting.

question.de: Hast du eine bekannte Erkrankung von Herz oder Blutgefäßen (auch nach Schlaganfall oder bei Durchblutungsstörungen der Beine), Diabetes (Typ 1 oder 2) oder eine Nierenerkrankung?
question.en: Do you have a known disease of the heart or blood vessels (including after a stroke or with poor circulation in the legs), diabetes (type 1 or 2) or kidney disease?

source.title: Whitfield GP, Riebe D, Magal M, Liguori G. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001–2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2017;49(10):2056–2063 (describes the algorithm of Riebe D et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015;47(11):2473–2479)

quote: relies on current exercise participation; history and symptoms of cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease […] Cardiac, peripheral vascular, or cerebrovascular disease. […] Type 1 and 2 diabetes mellitus.

summary.de: Schmerzen oder Beschwerden in Brust, Hals, Kiefer oder Armen (in Ruhe oder bei Belastung): ärztlich abklären.
summary.en: Pain or discomfort in the chest, neck, jaw or arms (at rest or during activity): get medical clearance.

question.de: Hast du in Ruhe oder bei Belastung Schmerzen, Druck oder ein Engegefühl in Brust, Hals, Kiefer oder Armen?
question.en: Do you have pain, pressure or tightness in your chest, neck, jaw or arms, at rest or during activity?

source.title: Whitfield GP, Riebe D, Magal M, Liguori G. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001–2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2017;49(10):2056–2063 (describes the algorithm of Riebe D et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015;47(11):2473–2479)

quote: At rest or during activity; includes pain, discomfort in the chest, neck, jaw, arms, or other areas that may result from ischemia;

summary.de: Schwindel oder Ohnmacht: ärztlich abklären.
summary.en: Dizziness or fainting: get medical clearance.

question.de: Hast du Schwindelanfälle oder bist du in letzter Zeit ohnmächtig geworden?
question.en: Do you have dizzy spells, or have you fainted recently?

source.title: Whitfield GP, Riebe D, Magal M, Liguori G. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001–2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2017;49(10):2056–2063 (describes the algorithm of Riebe D et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015;47(11):2473–2479)

quote: dizziness or syncope; orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea; ankle edema; palpitations or tachycardia;

summary.de: Atemnot in Ruhe oder bei leichter Anstrengung, nächtliche Atemnot oder geschwollene Knöchel: ärztlich abklären.
summary.en: Shortness of breath at rest or with mild exertion, breathlessness at night or swollen ankles: get medical clearance.

question.de: Bist du schon in Ruhe oder bei leichter Anstrengung ungewöhnlich kurzatmig, wachst du nachts mit Atemnot auf oder sind deine Knöchel geschwollen?
question.en: Are you unusually short of breath at rest or with light effort, do you wake up at night short of breath, or are your ankles swollen?

source.title: Whitfield GP, Riebe D, Magal M, Liguori G. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001–2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2017;49(10):2056–2063 (describes the algorithm of Riebe D et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015;47(11):2473–2479)

quote: orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea; ankle edema; […] shortness of breath at rest or with mild exertion

summary.de: Herzrasen oder Herzstolpern: ärztlich abklären.
summary.en: Palpitations or a racing heart: get medical clearance.

question.de: Hast du Herzrasen oder spürst du einen unregelmäßigen Herzschlag?
question.en: Do you have a racing heart or feel an irregular heartbeat?

source.title: Whitfield GP, Riebe D, Magal M, Liguori G. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001–2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2017;49(10):2056–2063 (describes the algorithm of Riebe D et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015;47(11):2473–2479)

quote: dizziness or syncope; orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea; ankle edema; palpitations or tachycardia;

summary.de: Wer Beschwerden hat oder (ohne regelmäßiges Training) eine bekannte Herz-Kreislauf-, Stoffwechsel- oder Nierenerkrankung, soll vor dem Training jeder Intensität ärztlich abklären lassen, ob er trainieren darf. Weekbeat wendet das auf jedes Ja an (strenger als die Quelle) und pausiert den Plan bis dahin.
summary.en: People with signs or symptoms, or (when not exercising regularly) a known cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease, should get medical clearance before exercise of any intensity. Weekbeat applies this to every yes (stricter than the source) and pauses the plan until then.

source.title: Whitfield GP, Riebe D, Magal M, Liguori G. Applying the ACSM Preparticipation Screening Algorithm to U.S. Adults: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2001–2004. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2017;49(10):2056–2063 (describes the algorithm of Riebe D et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015;47(11):2473–2479)

quote: Symptomatic respondents, regardless of history, are recommended to seek medical clearance before beginning exercise of any intensity […] Asymptomatic respondents with a positive history of the specified diseases are recommended to seek medical clearance before beginning exercise of any intensity […] Approval from a healthcare professional to engage in exercise.
